title: The row that keeps an earlier objective within its tolerance

blocks.text: A freight company plans its fleet with two prioritized objectives and solves them one at a time, because its solver does not take auxiliary objectives. After each objective $`f`$ is optimized to its best value $`\Gamma`$, a row must keep $`f`$ within its allowed loss of $`\Gamma`$ for every later solve. With the tolerances of a `mathopt.ObjectiveParameters` (either may be `None`):
A missing tolerance counts as 0, and `params=None` means a loss of 0.

Write `keep_within(model, expr, best, is_maximize, params)`, which adds that row to `model` for the linear expression `expr` and returns it. The tests fix the variables and ask HiGHS whether the model accepts the values, so any correct row passes. About eight lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from keep import keep_within


def accepts(value, best, is_maximize, params):
    model = mathopt.Model()
    margin = model.add_variable(lb=-1e6, ub=1e6, name="margin")
    keep_within(model, 3 * margin, best, is_maximize, params)
    margin.lower_bound = margin.upper_bound = value / 3
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    return result.termination.reason == mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL


REL2 = mathopt.ObjectiveParameters(objective_degradation_relative_tolerance=0.02)
ABS9 = mathopt.ObjectiveParameters(objective_degradation_absolute_tolerance=9)
print("max, best 600, 2 percent, value 588:", accepts(588, 600, True, REL2))
print("max, best 600, 2 percent, value 585:", accepts(585, 600, True, REL2))
print("min, best 300, absolute 9, value 309:", accepts(309, 300, False, ABS9))
print("min, best 300, no tolerance, value 301:", accepts(301, 300, False, None))

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


def keep_within(model: mathopt.Model, expr, best: float, is_maximize: bool,
                params: mathopt.ObjectiveParameters | None):
    """Add and return the row keeping `expr` within its allowed loss of `best`."""
    # TODO: the allowed loss, then a row whose direction follows the objective's sense.
    return None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = mathopt.Model()
    cost = model.add_variable(lb=-1e6, ub=1e6, name="cost")
    print(keep_within(model, cost, 1000, False, mathopt.ObjectiveParameters(objective_degradation_absolute_tolerance=5)))

a minimized objective with best 1,000 and an absolute tolerance of 5 allows 1,005 and 900 and refuses 1,006
with no parameters the objective must stay at its best value
a maximized objective with best -1,000 and a 1% tolerance allows -1,010 and refuses -1,011
with an absolute tolerance of 50 and a relative one of 1% on best 1,000, 950 is allowed and 949 refused
